agent.code.title: Request code
agent.code.hint: The agent shows the same code. Approve only if they match.
agent.unknownItems: This request names items that are not in your vaults on this device. Deny it, or sync and try again.
agent.prefixHint: Also with anything after it, but never chained with ; | & or redirections.
agent.pathsHint: The file is readable only by your user. The agent may be able to read it afterwards.
agent.duration.minutes: For {minutes, plural, one {# minute} other {# minutes}}
agent.expiresIn: Waits {seconds, plural, one {# more second} other {# more seconds}} for your answer
agent.expired: This request expired. Ask the agent to try again.
agent.warning: Read the command line. A command can send the secrets anywhere; approve only what you expect from the task you gave the agent.
agent.notify.title: An AI agent waits for your approval
agent.notify.body: Open Passbox to approve or deny the request.
agent.notify.offer: Get a notification when an agent waits while Passbox is in the background.
agent.pending.title: Waiting for you
agent.pending.description: Requests from AI agents connected with pbx mcp. They expire after 10 minutes.
agent.grants.title: Recent requests
agent.grants.description: Approved access ends at the time shown, when the agent stops, or when you revoke it.
agent.grants.noneHint: Connect Claude Code, Cursor, VS Code or another agent with pbx mcp and a service account.
agent.revokeBody: The agent can no longer use these secrets. A command that is already running is not stopped.
agent.events.title: Agent activity
agent.events.description: What agents did with your secrets. Commands are shown as their first word and a short fingerprint, never with values.
agent.setup.title: Connect an AI agent
agent.setup.description: Agents see titles and field names, never secret values, and need your approval here for every use.
agent.setup.step1: Create a service account with read access to a vault that holds only what the agent needs.
agent.setup.step2: Install pbx and add it to your agent as an MCP server, for example in Claude Code:
agent.setup.step3: Keep Passbox open on this or another device: approvals appear here.
agent.setup.more: Cursor, VS Code, Claude Desktop and Codex: see docs/architecture/ai-agents.md.
serviceAccount.title: Service accounts
serviceAccount.description: Machine identities for CI pipelines, servers and AI agents. Each has its own key, access to the vaults you choose, and never more access than you.
serviceAccount.noneHint: Create one for each machine or pipeline, so you can revoke them one by one.
serviceAccount.honest: A token gives whoever holds it the access shown here until you revoke it. Revoking stops it at once; what it already downloaded cannot be taken back.
serviceAccount.revokeBody: Its token stops working at once, for every machine that uses it. It stays in the list with its activity.
serviceAccount.deleteBody: The service account, its access and its activity are removed. Its token stops working. This cannot be undone.
serviceAccount.createDescription: Choose the smallest set of vaults. Read access is enough for most pipelines and agents.
serviceAccount.name: Name
serviceAccount.nameHint: For example “GitHub Actions deploy” or “Claude Code”. Visible to the server.
serviceAccount.vaultsHint: Read and write needs edit access to the vault yourself.
serviceAccount.expiryNeverHint: A token without expiry works until you revoke it. Prefer an expiry and create a new one when it ends.
serviceAccount.tokenDescription: Store it in your CI secret store or the agent's configuration now. It is shown only once.
serviceAccount.tokenWarning: Passbox does not keep this token and cannot show it again. If you lose it, create a new service account and delete this one.
serviceAccount.manageDescription: Changes apply at once. Removing a vault ends access to it.
serviceAccount.renewHint: The vault's key was changed. Renew so the service account can read items changed since.
